tridentiger.definition: tridentiger gērī, m tridens + GES-, the trident-bearer (of Neptune), O.

trifaux.definition: trifaux cis, adj. tres+faux, having three throats, triple-throated : latratus (Cerberi), V.

trini.definition: trīnī ae, a, num distr. tres, three each, three : circum Samorabrivam trinis hibernis hiemare, Cs.: litterae.—In the phrase, trinūm nundinūm, see nundinae.— Threefold, triple : trinis catenis vinctus, Cs.: Nomina, O.

tripertito.definition: tripertītō (-partītō) adv. tripartitus, in three parts, into three parts : bona dividere: equitatus, tripertito divisus, Cs.: urbem adgreditur, L.

tripertitus.definition: tripertītus (-partītus) Part. ter+partitus, divided into three parts, threefold, tripartite : ea causa tripertita erit in accusatione: tripertitas orbis terrarum oras notare.

tripes.definition: tripēs edis, adj. ter+pes, with three feet, three-footed : mensa, H.: mulus natus, L.

tripodes.definition: tripodēs um, m plur. of tripus.

tritura.definition: trītūra ae, f 1 TER-, a rubbing, chafing, threshing : Magna, V.

tritus1.definition: trītus adj. with comp. P. of tero, oft-trodden, beaten, frequented, common, worn : iter in Graeciam: Appia trita rotis, O.— Fig., practised, expert : aures.—Of language, much used, familiar, common, commonplace, trite…

tritus2.definition: (trītus, ūs) m 1 TER-, a rubbing down, wearing away (only abl.): lapidum tritu.

triumphans.definition: triumphāns antis, adj. P. of triumpho, triumphal, belonging to a triumph : equi, O.

triumvir.definition: triumvir or IIIvir virī, gen plur. ōrum or ū m, m tres+vir, one of three associates in office, a member of a board of three, one of three joint commissioners : Gracchum triumvirum coloniis deducundis necaverat, i. e. …

truculenter.definition: (truculenter) adv. truculentus, savagely, fiercely, ferociously .—Only comp: truculentius se gerebat.

truncus1.definition: truncus adj. TARC-, maimed, mutilated, mangled, dismembered, disfigured : Trunca manu pinus regit (Polyphemum), i. e. the trunk of a pinetree , V.: frons, without its horn , O.: corpus, limbless , O.: puerum trunci co…

trusito.definition: trūsitō —, —, āre to push often: mulum trusitant, Ph.

tubicen.definition: tubicen cinis, m tuba+1 CAN-, a trumpeter : cornicines tubicinesque canere iubet, L.: signa dedit tubicen, O.

tueo.definition: tueō —, —, ēre, collat. form of tueor, to care for, maintain: censores vectigalia tuento.

tumultuose.definition: tumultuōsē adv. with comp. and sup. tumultuosus, in confusion, disorderly, tumultuously : senatus tumultuose vocatus tumultuosius consulitur, L.: tumultuosius vagari, Cs.: hominem tumultuosissime adoriri.

tun.definition: tūn colloq. for tū-ne; see tu.

tunicatus.definition: tunicātus adj. tunica, clothed with a tunic, in shirt sleeves : ut exercitatione tunicati uteremur: popellus, i. e. without a toga , H.—Plur m . as subst: metus tunicatorum illorum? i. e. of the vulgar .

turbate.definition: turbātē adv. turbatus, in confusion, disorderly : aguntur omnia, Cs.

turbatus.definition: turbātus adj. P. of 1 turbo, troubled, disturbed, disordered, agitated, confused : oculis simul ac mente, L.: placare (voluntates) turbatas.

turbide.definition: turbidē adv. turbidus, in disorder, confusedly : omnia esse suscepta.

turbo2.definition: turbō inis, m 1 turbo, that which whirls, a whirlwind, hurricane, tornado : saevi exsistunt turbines, Pac. ap. C.: validi venti, O.: turbo aut subita tempestas: pulvis collectus turbine, H.: venti terras turbine perfl…

turbulente.definition: turbulentē adv. with comp. turbulentus, confusedly, tumultuously, boisterously : humana pati, composedly : egit de Caepione turbulentius.

turbulenter.definition: turbulenter adv. turbulentus, confusedly, tumultuously : nihil facere.

turgeo.definition: turgeō —, —, ēre, to swell out, be swollen, be tumid: turgentia ora (from the stings of hornets). O.: laeto in palmite gemmae, V.: sacculus pleno ore, Iu.—Fig., of speech, to be inflated, be turgid, be bombastic: prof…

turpiter.definition: turpiter adv. with comp. and sup. turpis, in an unsightly manner, repulsively : ut turpiter atrum Desinat in piscem mulier, H.: claudicare, O.—Fig., in an unseemly manner, basely, shamefully, disgracefully, dishonorab…

tute2.definition: tūtē adv. with comp. and sup. tutus, safely, securely, in safety, without danger : tutius receptus daretur, Cs.

tyrannice.definition: tyrannicē adv. tyrannicus, arbitrarily, tyrannically . ea quae tyrannice statuit.
